first.rationale: The two live symptoms are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), which are causally linked: onboarding completion feeds activation. memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (fewer signup fields lifted first-week activation) point at the same lever from two independent readouts, so simplify_onboarding is the direction with the most convergent inherited support and it attacks both symptoms with one slot. I verify memory_86 because it is the primary basis for the action I intend to take and I want the original record's effect size, segment, and durability window before committing the only slot this week. I verify memory_73 because promotional pricing is the obvious reflex against a competitor's entry pricing, and it is the one memory carrying an explicit self-flagged defect: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, meaning the reported acquisition/revenue lift may be an artifact of cohort mixing rather than a real effect. Given the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, acting on a possibly-inflated discount result would be the costliest error available, so it is worth spending the second pull to either rehabilitate or retire that option rather than leaving it as an unexamined temptation. Downstream value risk is real in both directions and I am flagging it: discounting into a price war buys volume that may not be qualified and can permanently reset price expectations; and even my intended action can degrade lead quality, since stripping signup fields can raise raw signups while lowering the share of accounts that ever become qualified revenue. I will therefore instrument the onboarding test on downstream qualified-conversion and retention, not just completion rate, and run it at standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout because memory_86 and memory_31 are archived summaries whose durability past the first week is not established. Uncertainty preserved: memory_57 (referrals) and memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist) remain plausible and unrefuted, but neither addresses the two metrics that are actually moving right now, and memory_91 (activation messaging) is a close second I would run next if the onboarding record comes back weaker than the summary implies. If verification shows memory_86's lift was confined to a segment that is not the one declining, I will switch to activation_messaging rather than defaulting to the pricing response.
